category: MATLAB Projects, Build Automation, Packaging & Deployment
description: Programmatic MATLAB project management, the MATLAB build tool (buildfile tasks for tests, code issues, MEX and P-code), toolbox packaging and add-on management, publishing/exporting code, and MATLAB Compiler / Compiler SDK functions that build standalone apps, web apps, Excel add-ins, Python/C++/Java/.NET components, installers and Docker images.

tools.name: currentProject
tools.description: Returns the matlab.project.Project object of the currently loaded MATLAB project. Use it in scripts to query project files, labels, paths and root folder, or to run project checks.
tools.notes: Errors if no project is loaded; matlab.project.currentProject returns empty instead (useful in startup code). Project paths are added when the project opens and removed when it closes.

tools.name: openProject
tools.description: Loads an existing MATLAB project from its root folder or .prj file, setting up the project path, running startup files and returning the project object. This is how CI jobs and batch scripts put a project's code on the path.

parameters.name: projectPath
parameters.description: Project root folder or path to the .prj file.

tools.notes: Opening a project closes any currently open project. Closing it (close(proj)) runs shutdown files and removes project paths. Use matlab.project.loadProject for a non-interactive load in older workflows.

tools.name: matlab.project.createProject
tools.description: Creates a new, blank MATLAB project in a folder (or the default location) and opens it. Follow up with addFile, addPath and addStartupFile to populate it programmatically.
tools.usage:
proj = matlab.project.createProject
proj = matlab.project.createProject(folder)
proj = matlab.project.createProject(Name=name, Folder=folder)

parameters.name: folder
parameters.description: Root folder for the new project (created if missing).

parameters.name: Name
parameters.description: Project name.

tools.notes: Fails if the folder already contains a project. To convert an existing folder, use the desktop's New > Project > From Folder or create the project in that folder and add its files.

tools.name: matlab.project.extractProject
tools.description: Extracts a project archive (.mlproj) created by exporting a project, and returns the path of the extracted project root. Use it to distribute and restore complete projects including references and settings.

parameters.name: archive
parameters.description: Path to the .mlproj file.

parameters.name: destination
parameters.description: Folder to extract into.

tools.notes: Introduced R2022b. export(proj, archiveName) creates the archive; set archive options such as including referenced projects when exporting.

tools.name: addFile
tools.description: Adds a file or folder (without its children) to a MATLAB project and returns the corresponding ProjectFile object. Only files that belong to the project are tracked for dependencies, labels and source control.

parameters.name: proj
parameters.description: Project object from currentProject/openProject.

parameters.name: fileOrFolder
parameters.description: Path of the file or folder, absolute or relative to the project root.

tools.notes: Use addFolderIncludingChildFiles for whole folders and removeFile to remove. The project method addPath (distinct from the global addpath function) puts a project folder on the project path.

tools.name: addFolderIncludingChildFiles
tools.description: Adds a folder and all of its files and subfolders to a MATLAB project in one call. It is the quickest way to register an existing source tree with a project.

parameters.name: folder
parameters.description: Folder path to add recursively.

tools.notes: Adding files does not put them on the MATLAB path; also add the relevant folders to the project path.

tools.name: addStartupFile
tools.description: Registers a script or function to run automatically every time the project opens, for example to set preferences, load configuration or check prerequisites. addShutdownFile registers cleanup code run on close.

parameters.name: file
parameters.description: Project file (.m, .mlx, .p) to run at startup or shutdown.

tools.notes: Startup files run after the project path is set. Remove with removeStartupFile/removeShutdownFile. Since R2025a listStartupIssues reports problems encountered during startup.

tools.name: addReference
tools.description: Adds another MATLAB project as a referenced project, so that its path and startup behavior are included when the parent project opens. Referencing lets teams compose components without copying code.

parameters.name: folder
parameters.description: Root folder of the project to reference.

parameters.name: referenceType
parameters.description: "relative" (default) or "absolute" path storage.

tools.notes: Relative references keep the project portable across machines and repositories checked out side by side. Remove with removeReference.

tools.name: listModifiedFiles
tools.description: Lists project files that have local modifications according to the project's source control integration (Git or SVN). Useful in pre-commit checks and for running only affected tests.

parameters.name: proj
parameters.description: Project under source control.

tools.notes: Call refreshSourceControl(proj) first if files changed outside MATLAB. listImpactedFiles finds files affected by those changes through the dependency graph.

tools.name: listRequiredFiles
tools.description: Returns the files required by specified project files according to the project dependency analysis. Use it to find what must be shipped or tested along with a given entry point.

parameters.name: files
parameters.description: Project file path(s) whose dependencies to list.

tools.notes: Run updateDependencies first for up-to-date results. Outside projects use matlab.codetools.requiredFilesAndProducts. The Dependency Analyzer app visualizes the graph.

tools.name: runChecks
tools.description: Runs the project integrity checks (files on path are in the project, derived files, source control consistency, references, etc.) and returns the results. Suitable for CI gating of project health.

parameters.name: proj
parameters.description: Project object.

tools.notes: Each result has ID, Description, Passed and ProblemFiles. Some checks require dependency analysis to have been run.

tools.name: buildtool
tools.description: Runs tasks defined in the project's buildfile.m using the MATLAB build tool, resolving task dependencies and skipping up-to-date tasks. It is the standard entry point for CI pipelines (test, lint, package).
tools.usage:
buildtool
buildtool task1 ... taskN
buildtool ___ -continueOnFailure -skip task -parallel -verbosity level
buildtool -tasks
buildtool -init

parameters.name: tasks
parameters.description: Task names; arguments can be passed, e.g. test("folder",Option="value").

parameters.name: -continueOnFailure
parameters.description: Keep running remaining tasks after a failure (R2023b+).

parameters.name: -skip
parameters.description: Skip a named task (R2023b+).

parameters.name: -parallel
parameters.description: Run tasks in parallel (R2024a+, requires Parallel Computing Toolbox).

parameters.name: -tasks / -init
parameters.description: List tasks with descriptions; create a starter buildfile.m.

tools.example:
% shell:  matlab -batch "buildtool check test"
buildtool -tasks
buildtool test -verbosity Detailed
tools.notes: Introduced R2022b. Searches the current and parent folders for buildfile.m. A failing task makes matlab -batch exit with a non-zero code, which CI systems detect.

tools.name: buildplan
tools.description: Creates a matlab.buildtool.Plan, typically inside buildfile.m, optionally turning local functions whose names end in "Task" into tasks. The plan holds the tasks, their dependencies and the default tasks.

parameters.name: fcns
parameters.description: Cell array of function handles, usually localfunctions; functions named xxxTask become task "xxx" with the first help line as description.

tools.notes: Introduced R2022b. Built-in task classes live in matlab.buildtool.tasks. Task functions receive a matlab.buildtool.TaskContext argument.

tools.name: matlab.buildtool.Task
tools.description: Class representing a single unit of work in a build plan, with actions, a description, dependencies and optional inputs/outputs for incremental builds. Create tasks directly when a function-based task is not flexible enough.

parameters.name: Description
parameters.description: Text shown by buildtool -tasks.

parameters.name: Dependencies
parameters.description: Names of tasks that must run first.

parameters.name: Actions
parameters.description: Function handle(s) taking a TaskContext.

parameters.name: Inputs / Outputs
parameters.description: Files or FileCollections used for up-to-date checks.

tools.example:
plan("docs") = matlab.buildtool.Task( ...
    Description="Export live scripts to HTML", ...
    Inputs="doc/*.mlx", Outputs="html/*.html", ...
    Actions=@(ctx) arrayfun(@(f) export(f.Path, Format="html"), ctx.Task.Inputs.paths));
tools.notes: When Inputs and Outputs are set, the task is skipped if nothing changed since the last successful run. TaskGroup organizes related tasks.

tools.name: matlab.buildtool.tasks.TestTask
tools.description: Built-in build task that runs MATLAB tests and can produce JUnit/HTML test reports and code coverage (Cobertura XML or HTML). It fails the build if any test fails.
tools.usage:
task = matlab.buildtool.tasks.TestTask
task = matlab.buildtool.tasks.TestTask(tests)
task = matlab.buildtool.tasks.TestTask(___, Name=Value)

parameters.name: tests
parameters.description: Test files or folders (default: project test files or current folder).

parameters.name: SourceFiles
parameters.description: Code under test; enables incremental runs and coverage.

parameters.name: TestResults
parameters.description: Report paths (.xml JUnit, .html, .pdf, .mat).

parameters.name: CodeCoverageResults
parameters.description: Coverage report paths (.xml Cobertura, .html, .mat).

parameters.name: Tag / Strict / OutputDetail / IncludeSubfolders
parameters.description: Selection, warnings-as-failures, verbosity, recursion.

tools.notes: Introduced R2023b. Parallel test runs via buildtool -parallel. RunOnlyImpactedTests requires MATLAB Test (R2025a+).

tools.name: matlab.buildtool.tasks.CodeIssuesTask
tools.description: Built-in build task that analyzes source code with the Code Analyzer (codeIssues), reports findings and fails the build when errors (or, optionally, warnings) exceed thresholds. Results can be exported in SARIF format for CI code-scanning dashboards.

parameters.name: sourceFiles
parameters.description: Files or folders to analyze (default: project or current folder).

parameters.name: Results
parameters.description: Output file(s), e.g. "results/issues.sarif" or .mat.

parameters.name: ErrorThreshold / WarningThreshold
parameters.description: Maximum allowed errors/warnings before the task fails.

tools.notes: Introduced R2023b. Equivalent interactive analysis: codeIssues(folder) or the Code Analyzer report.

tools.name: matlab.buildtool.tasks.CleanTask
tools.description: Built-in build task that deletes the outputs and incremental-build traces of other tasks in the plan, forcing them to rerun on the next build.
tools.example:
plan("clean") = matlab.buildtool.tasks.CleanTask;
% shell: matlab -batch "buildtool clean test"
tools.notes: Introduced R2023b. Only outputs declared via task Outputs are removed.

tools.name: matlab.buildtool.tasks.MexTask
tools.description: Built-in build task that compiles C/C++/Fortran source files into a MEX file, rebuilding only when sources change. Lets native extensions be part of the automated build.

parameters.name: sourceFiles
parameters.description: Source files to compile and link.

parameters.name: outputFolder
parameters.description: Folder for the MEX binary.

parameters.name: Filename
parameters.description: Name of the MEX file to build.

parameters.name: Options
parameters.description: Extra mex options, e.g. ["-R2018a" "-silent"].

tools.notes: Introduced R2024a; MexTask.forEachFile (R2025a) creates a task group with one MEX per source file. Requires a supported compiler (mex -setup).

tools.name: matlab.buildtool.tasks.PcodeTask
tools.description: Built-in build task that obfuscates MATLAB source files into P-code in an output folder, with incremental rebuilds. Use it when packaging toolboxes that should not expose source.
tools.usage:
task = matlab.buildtool.tasks.PcodeTask(source, outputFolder)
task = matlab.buildtool.tasks.PcodeTask(source, outputFolder, Name=Value)

parameters.name: Algorithm
parameters.description: "R2022a" (stronger, default) or "R2007b" obfuscation.

parameters.name: PreserveSourceFolder
parameters.description: Keep the source folder name in the output structure.

tools.notes: Introduced R2024a. Equivalent to calling pcode manually. Help text is removed; ship separate help .m files if needed.

tools.name: pcode
tools.description: Creates obfuscated, execute-only P-code (.p) files from MATLAB .m files or folders. The P-file runs like the original but its source cannot be read, and it takes precedence over a same-named .m file.

parameters.name: item
parameters.description: File, folder or wildcard of .m files.

parameters.name: -inplace
parameters.description: Write P-files next to the sources instead of the current folder.

parameters.name: -R2022a / -R2007b
parameters.description: Obfuscation algorithm; -R2022a is more robust (default in recent releases).

tools.example:
pcode("src/*.m", "-inplace")
which myAlgorithm   % shows the .p file
tools.notes: P-code is obfuscation, not encryption; MATLAB Compiler offers stronger protection. Files produced with -R2022a need R2022a or later to run.

tools.name: matlab.addons.toolbox.packageToolbox
tools.description: Packages a toolbox into a single installable .mltbx file from a toolbox project (.prj) or a ToolboxOptions object. Recipients install it with a double-click or installToolbox.

parameters.name: projectFile
parameters.description: Toolbox packaging project (.prj) created with the Package Toolbox dialog.

parameters.name: outputFile
parameters.description: Name/location of the .mltbx file.

parameters.name: opts
parameters.description: matlab.addons.toolbox.ToolboxOptions object (R2023a+) for fully scripted packaging.

tools.notes: The identifier must stay constant across versions so upgrades replace older installs. Combine with a buildtool task for automated releases.

tools.name: matlab.addons.toolbox.installToolbox
tools.description: Installs a .mltbx toolbox file into the current MATLAB installation's add-ons folder and adds it to the path. Use it for scripted environment setup and CI agents.

parameters.name: toolboxFile
parameters.description: Path to the .mltbx file.

parameters.name: agreeToLicense
parameters.description: true to accept the toolbox license non-interactively.

tools.notes: matlab.addons.install is not recommended; prefer this function. Uninstall with matlab.addons.toolbox.uninstallToolbox.

tools.name: matlab.addons.installedAddons
tools.description: Returns a table of installed add-ons (toolboxes, apps, support packages, community toolboxes) with name, version, enabled state and identifier. Useful for checking prerequisites at runtime.
tools.notes: Enable or disable versions with matlab.addons.enableAddon/disableAddon and check with matlab.addons.isAddonEnabled. For MathWorks products also see ver and license('test',...).

tools.name: matlab.codetools.requiredFilesAndProducts
tools.description: Performs dependency analysis on MATLAB program files and returns the user files and MathWorks products they require. Use it to check which toolboxes (licenses) and files a program needs before sharing or deploying.

parameters.name: files
parameters.description: File name(s) to analyze.

parameters.name: "toponly"
parameters.description: Only report direct dependencies of the given files.

tools.notes: Static analysis cannot see functions called through eval or string-built names. pList includes Name, Version, ProductNumber and Certain.

tools.name: publish
tools.description: Runs a MATLAB script or function file and publishes the code, formatted comments and output (including figures) as an HTML, PDF, Word, LaTeX, PowerPoint or XML document. Handy for batch-generated reports from plain .m files.
tools.usage:
mydoc = publish(file)
mydoc = publish(file, format)
mydoc = publish(file, options)
mydoc = publish(file, Name, Value)

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: "html" (default), "pdf", "doc", "latex", "ppt" or "xml".

parameters.name: outputDir
parameters.description: Output folder (default ./html).

parameters.name: evalCode / showCode
parameters.description: Whether to run the code and include it in the output.

parameters.name: imageFormat / maxOutputLines / codeToEvaluate
parameters.description: Figure format, output truncation, and code used to call functions.

tools.example:
out = publish("analysis.m", format="pdf", outputDir="reports", showCode=false);
web(out)   % or winopen(out)
tools.notes: Use %% section breaks and markup in comments for structure. For Live Scripts use export instead. In matlab -batch, figures are still captured.

tools.name: export
tools.description: Converts a Live Script or Live Function (.mlx) to another format such as PDF, Word, HTML, LaTeX, Markdown, Jupyter notebook or plain .m code, optionally running it first so outputs are current.
tools.usage:
exportedFile = export(file)
exportedFile = export(file, formattedFile)
exportedFile = export(___, Name=Value)

parameters.name: file
parameters.description: Live script (.mlx) to convert.

parameters.name: formattedFile
parameters.description: Output file; its extension selects the format.

parameters.name: Format
parameters.description: "pdf", "docx", "html", "latex", "m", "markdown" or "ipynb" (Markdown/ipynb R2023b+).

parameters.name: Run
parameters.description: true to run the script before exporting.

tools.notes: Introduced R2022a. Works headless, making Live Scripts usable in automated report pipelines. The project method export(proj, ...) is different and creates .mlproj archives.

tools.name: coder.config
tools.description: Creates a MATLAB Coder configuration object for MEX, static library, dynamic library or executable code generation. Its properties control target language, optimization, reports and hardware settings, and it is passed to codegen with -config.
tools.usage:
cfg = coder.config(buildType)
cfg = coder.config(buildType, "ecoder", true)
cfg = coder.config("gpu")

parameters.name: buildType
parameters.description: "mex", "lib", "dll" or "exe".

parameters.name: "ecoder", true
parameters.description: Create an Embedded Coder configuration (requires Embedded Coder).

parameters.name: TargetLang / GenerateReport / EnableOpenMP
parameters.description: Common properties to set on the returned object.

tools.notes: Requires MATLAB Coder. Use coder.gpuConfig for GPU Coder and coder.screener to check code for unsupported functions before generating.

tools.name: compiler.build.standaloneApplication
tools.description: Builds a standalone console executable from a MATLAB function or script with MATLAB Compiler, returning a compiler.build.Results object. The executable runs on machines with the free MATLAB Runtime instead of MATLAB.

parameters.name: AppFile
parameters.description: Main .m/.mlx/.mlapp file.

parameters.name: ExecutableName / OutputDir
parameters.description: Name of the executable and build folder.

parameters.name: AdditionalFiles
parameters.description: Data files or folders to include.

parameters.name: TreatInputsAsNumeric
parameters.description: Convert command-line arguments to numbers.

parameters.name: Verbose / AutoDetectDataFiles
parameters.description: Build output and automatic data file inclusion.

tools.notes: Introduced R2020b as a scriptable alternative to mcc -m. Command-line arguments arrive as char vectors unless TreatInputsAsNumeric is set. Use isdeployed to branch on deployed-only behavior.

tools.name: compiler.build.standaloneWindowsApplication
tools.description: Builds a Windows standalone application that does not open a command window, intended for GUI programs such as App Designer apps. Supports custom icons and splash screens.

parameters.name: AppFile
parameters.description: Main app file, typically .mlapp.

parameters.name: ExecutableName / ExecutableIcon / ExecutableSplashScreen
parameters.description: Branding options.

parameters.name: OutputDir / AdditionalFiles
parameters.description: Build folder and extra files.

tools.notes: Windows only. Output from disp/fprintf is not visible; log to a file instead.

tools.name: compiler.build.webAppArchive
tools.description: Packages an App Designer app (.mlapp) into a web app archive (.ctf) for hosting on MATLAB Web App Server, where users run it in a browser.

parameters.name: AppFile
parameters.description: App Designer .mlapp file.

parameters.name: ArchiveName / OutputDir
parameters.description: Archive name and build folder.

parameters.name: AdditionalFiles
parameters.description: Data or helper files required by the app.

tools.example:
compiler.build.webAppArchive("myDashboard.mlapp", OutputDir="webapps");
% copy webapps/myDashboard.ctf to the Web App Server apps folder
tools.notes: Requires MATLAB Compiler; hosting requires MATLAB Web App Server. File dialogs and some desktop-only functions behave differently in web apps.

tools.name: compiler.build.excelAddIn
tools.description: Builds a Microsoft Excel add-in from MATLAB functions so that they can be called as worksheet formulas or from VBA macros, running on the MATLAB Runtime.

parameters.name: FunctionFiles
parameters.description: MATLAB functions to expose.

parameters.name: AddInName / ClassName / AddInVersion
parameters.description: Names and version of the COM add-in.

parameters.name: GenerateVisualBasicFile
parameters.description: Also generate the .bas VBA module.

tools.notes: Windows only and requires a supported C++ compiler. For Excel clients of MATLAB Production Server use compiler.build.excelClientForProductionServer.

tools.name: compiler.build.pythonPackage
tools.description: Builds a Python package from MATLAB functions with MATLAB Compiler SDK. Python code imports the package, initializes it and calls the MATLAB functions, which run on the MATLAB Runtime without a MATLAB license.

parameters.name: FunctionFiles
parameters.description: MATLAB functions to include.

parameters.name: PackageName
parameters.description: Python package name, may be dotted (e.g. "mycompany.mymagic").

parameters.name: OutputDir / AdditionalFiles / SampleGenerationFiles
parameters.description: Build folder, data files and MATLAB scripts from which Python samples are generated.

tools.example:
compiler.build.pythonPackage("magicsquare.m", PackageName="mymagic", OutputDir="pybuild");
% then in a shell:  cd pybuild && pip install .
% Python:
%   import mymagic
%   h = mymagic.initialize()
%   print(h.magicsquare(4))
%   h.terminate()
tools.notes: Requires MATLAB Compiler SDK. The Python version must be supported by the MATLAB release. Unlike the MATLAB Engine API, no MATLAB installation is needed on the target, only the Runtime.

tools.name: compiler.build.cppSharedLibrary
tools.description: Builds a C++ shared library (with generated header and wrapper code) from MATLAB functions using MATLAB Compiler SDK, for integration into C++ applications via the MATLAB Data API or the legacy mwArray API.

parameters.name: LibraryName
parameters.description: Name of the generated library.

parameters.name: Interface
parameters.description: "matlab-data" (default, modern C++ API) or "mwarray".

parameters.name: OutputDir / AdditionalFiles / SampleGenerationFiles
parameters.description: Build folder, extra files and sample sources.

tools.notes: Requires MATLAB Compiler SDK and a supported C++ compiler. With the MATLAB Data API the library is loaded at run time through matlab::cpplib::initMATLABLibrary.

tools.name: compiler.build.javaPackage
tools.description: Builds a Java package (JAR with generated classes) from MATLAB functions using MATLAB Compiler SDK, so Java applications can call them through MWArray or MATLAB Data API types.
tools.usage:
compiler.build.javaPackage(Files)
results = compiler.build.javaPackage(Files, Name=Value)
results = compiler.build.javaPackage(ClassMap)

parameters.name: Files / ClassMap
parameters.description: Functions to include, or a containers.Map grouping functions into classes.

parameters.name: PackageName / ClassName
parameters.description: Java package namespace and class name.

parameters.name: Interface
parameters.description: "mwarray" (default) or "matlab-data".

tools.notes: Requires MATLAB Compiler SDK and a JDK. Add javabuilder.jar from the MATLAB Runtime to the Java classpath at run time.

tools.name: compiler.build.dotNETAssembly
tools.description: Builds a .NET assembly from MATLAB functions with MATLAB Compiler SDK, callable from C# and other .NET languages via the MWArray API or the MATLAB Data API for .NET.
tools.usage:
compiler.build.dotNETAssembly(Files)
results = compiler.build.dotNETAssembly(Files, Name=Value)
results = compiler.build.dotNETAssembly(ClassMap)

parameters.name: AssemblyName / ClassName / AssemblyVersion
parameters.description: Namespace, class and version of the assembly.

parameters.name: Interface
parameters.description: "mwarray" or "matlab-data".

parameters.name: FrameworkVersion / EmbedArchive
parameters.description: Target framework and whether to embed the deployable archive.

tools.notes: Requires MATLAB Compiler SDK. .NET Core/.NET 5+ targets use the matlab-data interface on supported releases.

tools.name: compiler.build.productionServerArchive
tools.description: Builds a deployable archive (.ctf) of MATLAB functions for MATLAB Production Server, which exposes them to clients through RESTful JSON and language-specific client APIs.

parameters.name: FunctionFiles
parameters.description: Functions to deploy.

parameters.name: ArchiveName / OutputDir
parameters.description: Name of the .ctf and build folder.

parameters.name: FunctionSignatures
parameters.description: JSON file describing argument types for discovery and validation.

tools.notes: Requires MATLAB Compiler SDK; hosting requires MATLAB Production Server. compiler.package.microserviceDockerImage turns the archive into a microservice container.

tools.name: compiler.package.installer
tools.description: Creates an installer for files generated by MATLAB Compiler or Compiler SDK builds, optionally bundling the MATLAB Runtime or downloading it from the web during installation.
tools.usage:
compiler.package.installer(results)
compiler.package.installer(results, Name=Value)
compiler.package.installer(files, filePath, ApplicationName=appName)

parameters.name: results
parameters.description: compiler.build.Results from a build function.

parameters.name: InstallerName / OutputDir
parameters.description: Installer file name and location.

parameters.name: RuntimeDelivery
parameters.description: "web" (download at install), "installer" (bundled) or "none".

parameters.name: ApplicationName / Version / AuthorName / AuthorCompany / Summary
parameters.description: Metadata shown by the installer.

tools.notes: Bundled Runtime makes installers large (GBs) but offline-capable. compiler.runtime.customInstaller builds a reduced Runtime installer.

tools.name: compiler.package.docker
tools.description: Creates a Docker image containing a compiled standalone application and the MATLAB Runtime, so it can run in containers and orchestration platforms.
tools.usage:
compiler.package.docker(results)
compiler.package.docker(results, Name=Value)
compiler.package.docker(files, filepath, ImageName=imageName)

parameters.name: ImageName
parameters.description: Name of the Docker image.

parameters.name: DockerContext
parameters.description: Folder in which the Dockerfile and build context are written.

parameters.name: ExecuteDockerBuild
parameters.description: "on" (default) to run docker build, "off" to only generate the context.

parameters.name: AdditionalPackages / AdditionalInstructions / ContainerUser
parameters.description: Customize the generated Dockerfile.

tools.notes: Linux only, standalone applications only; Docker must be installed. compiler.runtime.createDockerImage builds a Runtime-only base image.

tools.name: compiler.runtime.customInstaller
tools.description: Creates a MATLAB Runtime installer containing only the components needed by specific compiled artifacts, significantly reducing download and disk size compared with the full Runtime.

parameters.name: results / filepath
parameters.description: Build results or requiredMCRProducts.txt / buildresult.json path.

parameters.name: RuntimeDelivery
parameters.description: "web" (default) or "installer".

parameters.name: OutputDir / PackageType
parameters.description: Output folder and "auto" or "zip" packaging.

tools.notes: Introduced R2024b. The custom Runtime only supports the artifacts it was built for.

tools.name: isdeployed
tools.description: Returns true when code is running as a deployed application on the MATLAB Runtime and false inside MATLAB. Use it to switch file paths, skip interactive code or avoid path changes in compiled apps.
tools.notes: ismcc returns true while the code is being analyzed by mcc. Deployed apps cannot use addpath/cd to load functions that were not compiled in.

tools.name: ctfroot
tools.description: Returns the root folder of the extracted deployable archive of a compiled application, where the packaged MATLAB files and data files live at run time.
tools.notes: Inside MATLAB it returns matlabroot. Files added with AdditionalFiles keep their relative structure under the archive root.

tools.name: mcrversion
tools.description: Returns the version numbers of the MATLAB Runtime that matches the running MATLAB release (or the Runtime a deployed application is using). Useful for diagnostics and compatibility checks.
tools.example:
[maj, mnr, upd] = mcrversion;
fprintf("MATLAB Runtime %d.%d update %d\n", maj, mnr, upd)
tools.notes: The Runtime version must match the release used to compile the application. version and ver report MATLAB's own version.
